main_body: two-story half-timbered tavern building with tiled roof
top_band: orange-brown tiled roof slope and ridge from row 0 to row 43
evidence: The building shows a large foreshortened tiled roof slope from rows 0-43 sitting above the two-story vertical front wall (rows 44-95). Under the roof eave (row 43) there is a distinct eave shadow on the plaster wall (rows 44-45), and the doorway and windows are recessed with sills and frames.

style.evidence: Compared to the Beodeul reference houses, the candidate's roof tiles are large, blocky, repetitive rectangles with black outlines on the sloped edges, lacking the fine diagonal scalloped tile pattern and rich multi-tone contrast of the reference. The plaster walls have large areas of nearly flat beige fill with very faint, sparse single-pixel dots rather than the crisp, high-contrast speckle and diagonal timber bracing of the reference. The chimney is a flat grey box with minimal brick texture compared to the richly textured brick chimney on the left reference.
